caveats: COUNTERFACTUAL — this position was not held

Rates are realized — derived by differencing Venus's borrowIndex accumulator, never from supplyRatePerBlock(), whose conversion to an annual figure needs a blocks-per-year constant that is not readable from chain and whose plausible values span 6.67x (A12, P-22).
The switching boundary is the myopic break-even, widened by a published margin. It is not a solved free boundary (A13).
Switch cost uses the full pool fee, not the LP's share of it: a router paying to swap pays PancakeSwap's protocol cut too (P-1).

A pool venue is quoted NET of its convexity cost — realized fees minus the LVR the same window actually booked. The gross fee APR is the number every other venue quotes, and ranking it against a lending market's net supply rate would let it win on a subtraction it had not made (A10, A21).

These are not the same risk. A supplied dollar earns a dollar rate and its principal stays a dollar. An LP range earns a rate measured in the pool's own quote token, and its principal is two assets whose value moves with the price — so a higher figure is not simply better, and the two numbers are not interchangeable however carefully each is derived.

There is no width-free fee APR: two LPs in one pool at one moment earn differently because they chose differently. Each range here is quoted at the width `make pools` measured as the leader over this tape, and `pools.json` records that the lead is not separated at this sample size (A21, A23).

A window holding fewer than 30 swaps has no verdict rather than a small number, and A1's ceiling is a fraction of the pool's own depth over the quoted range — so a range can pay well and still be refused for being too shallow to take the position.
2 market(s) have no NewReserveFactor row on the tape; 0.1 was used and the card says so per venue.

finding: Router supplied and then moved 1 time(s). Over 250h the best realized dollar rate was 2.98%, and the largest gap between the two venues reached 1.074pp against a round-trip hurdle of 1.059pp — so the edge cleared, and only just. It held the better-paying venue on 68% of samples, earning 6.15 against 1.0304 of cost. A boundary that is crossed narrowly is the interesting case: the same agent declined to move on a 0.3pp edge earlier in this tape.
pool_finding: Router measured 2 PancakeSwap range(s) as venues and entered none of them, and the reason is size rather than yield. A1 caps a replayed position at 1% of the venue it sits in, and against a notional of 10,000 the ceilings are: PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.05% at +/-80 ticks tops out at 2,485; PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.25% at +/-400 ticks tops out at 185. The fee APR was measured and is on the card; what the ranges could not do is absorb this much capital without moving the price the replay is priced against. At a smaller notional the same policy over the same tape reaches a different answer, which is why the ceiling is published beside each range rather than the refusal alone.

quote.basis: net return on supplied capital (realized yield − switch costs), over 125h — too short to annualise honestly

venue: Venus Core Pool (BSC) dollar markets and 2 PancakeSwap v3 range(s) at +/-80, +/-400 ticks
